steps.title: Prepare the surface
steps.action: Start with a smooth, fully dry black primer. Place one broad light above and in front of your model.
steps.detail: Remove visible mould lines before priming. Follow the primer label for application and curing; brush-on colour is not a substitute for primer. Tilt the model under your light and choose the upper edges you will keep brightest. Begin on one test miniature before committing a squad.
steps.lookFor: Clean relief, open recesses and no grainy patches in the primer.
steps.simpleExplanation: A smooth starting surface makes thin paint easier to control. Choose the light before adding highlights.

steps.title: Build the foundation
steps.action: Apply Abaddon Black to the armour, joints and weapon casing.
steps.detail: Even over black primer, brush on a thin, even coat so later corrections match the same finish. Work around rivets rather than flooding them; broad plates should remain smooth.
steps.lookFor: An even black field, with all rivets and seams still visible.
steps.simpleExplanation: Keep the layer smooth and let it dry before adding more Abaddon Black.

steps.title: Place the light
steps.action: Trace Eshin Grey along the shoulder rims, helmet brow and knee edges.
steps.detail: Start on the shoulder edge where the side of your brush can catch the ridge. Keep the lines narrow on the lower legs and slightly stronger around the face. Do not fill the plate centres.
steps.lookFor: Black dominates every panel; grey describes the silhouette.
steps.simpleExplanation: Touch the edge with the side of the brush. Make the brightest marks the smallest.

steps.title: Refine the brightest edges
steps.action: Add short Dawnstone marks inside the uppermost grey edges.
steps.detail: Change direction with the form. A small corner point and a short helmet-brow line are enough to establish the light; avoid a complete pale outline around every plate.
steps.lookFor: The helmet reads first, without turning the armour grey.
steps.simpleExplanation: Touch the edge with the side of the brush. Make the brightest marks the smallest.

steps.title: Add the red heraldry
steps.action: Block chosen weapon and heraldic areas in Mephiston Red, then edge with Evil Sunz Scarlet.
steps.detail: Keep your design consistent across the miniature. Paint a simple red panel before attempting fine heraldic patterns. Correct any spill into the armour with Abaddon Black after the red has dried.
steps.lookFor: Crisp red areas sit within the black design.
steps.simpleExplanation: Separate the red shape cleanly before adding a smaller bright edge.

steps.title: Finish the contrasts
steps.action: Paint exposed machinery with Leadbelcher and shade its joints with Nuln Oil.
steps.detail: Keep metallic particles out of the red and black by rinsing your brush and changing the water. Restore a little Leadbelcher on raised mechanical edges after the shade dries.
steps.lookFor: Metal reads as a separate material, with dark gaps.
steps.simpleExplanation: Paint each material separately. Let it dry before working against its boundary.

steps.title: Check the whole miniature
steps.action: Look at the model at arm’s length, then rotate it under the same light. Correct the one area that interrupts the scheme most.
steps.detail: Use the original colour to narrow any over-wide highlight or untidy boundary. Keep lower-facing surfaces quieter than the head and upper surfaces. Let all acrylic layers dry before handling. Transfers, the scenic base and varnish are separate finishing choices; this walkthrough covers the main miniature colour scheme.
steps.lookFor: The main colour reads first; details support it without covering the shadows.
steps.simpleExplanation: Stop when the shapes and materials are clear. More highlights are not always an improvement.

steps.title: Prepare the surface
steps.action: Start with a smooth, fully dry black primer. Place one broad light above and in front of your model.
steps.detail: Remove visible mould lines before priming. Follow the primer label for application and curing; brush-on colour is not a substitute for primer. Tilt the model under your light and choose the upper edges you will keep brightest. Begin on one test miniature before committing a squad.
steps.lookFor: Clean relief, open recesses and no grainy patches in the primer.
steps.simpleExplanation: A smooth starting surface makes thin paint easier to control. Choose the light before adding highlights.

steps.title: Build the foundation
steps.action: Apply Abaddon Black to the armour and weapon casing.
steps.detail: Create a consistent surface over the primer so corrections do not leave different patches of finish. Keep brush pressure light around sharp shoulder rims.
steps.lookFor: A smooth black field with all fine relief preserved.
steps.simpleExplanation: Keep the layer smooth and let it dry before adding more Abaddon Black.

steps.title: Place the light
steps.action: Sketch Dark Reaper along the upper armour edges.
steps.detail: Use the side of the brush where a ridge is accessible. Where it is not, rotate the miniature and pull a short line toward yourself. Leave the broad centres fully black.
steps.lookFor: Cool outlines reveal the armour without turning it blue.
steps.simpleExplanation: Touch the edge with the side of the brush. Make the brightest marks the smallest.

steps.title: Refine the brightest edges
steps.action: Place short Thunderhawk Blue accents on the brow, shoulder corners and upper knees.
steps.detail: Keep this line thinner and shorter than the darker line beneath it. If a line becomes broad, let it dry and narrow it with Abaddon Black.
steps.lookFor: A few cool bright points draw attention to the upper body.
steps.simpleExplanation: Touch the edge with the side of the brush. Make the brightest marks the smallest.

steps.title: Keep the heraldry quiet
steps.action: Paint selected insignia in Corax White and lenses in Mephiston Red.
steps.detail: Use small, smooth strokes to establish the shape of the insignia. A large white block changes the balance of the model, so keep this study to existing small markings rather than adding whole white panels.
steps.lookFor: Pale markings remain crisp and controlled.
steps.simpleExplanation: Small white and red shapes are enough to break up the black.

steps.title: Finish the contrasts
steps.action: Pick out steel fittings with Leadbelcher and shade their recesses with Nuln Oil.
steps.detail: Keep steel separate from the cool blue-grey armour light. Once dry, restore Leadbelcher to raised mechanical edges, leaving the crevices dark.
steps.lookFor: Metal looks reflective; the armour remains visually quiet.
steps.simpleExplanation: Paint each material separately. Let it dry before working against its boundary.

steps.title: Check the whole miniature
steps.action: Look at the model at arm’s length, then rotate it under the same light. Correct the one area that interrupts the scheme most.
steps.detail: Use the original colour to narrow any over-wide highlight or untidy boundary. Keep lower-facing surfaces quieter than the head and upper surfaces. Let all acrylic layers dry before handling. Transfers, the scenic base and varnish are separate finishing choices; this walkthrough covers the main miniature colour scheme.
steps.lookFor: The main colour reads first; details support it without covering the shadows.
steps.simpleExplanation: Stop when the shapes and materials are clear. More highlights are not always an improvement.

steps.action: Apply Khorne Red to the armour.

steps.title: Separate the forms

steps.title: Recover the colour
steps.action: Return with Khorne Red across the broad crimson panels.

steps.title: Place the light

steps.title: Choose three distinct identities
steps.action: Label three separate parts: Iron Hands, Salamanders and Raven Guard. Place them beneath the same broad light.
steps.detail: Choose similarly shaped pieces so you can compare the colour treatment. The reference describes these Legions fighting together after Isstvan V; it does not give them one shared uniform. Keep each part’s Legion identity separate throughout this study.
steps.lookFor: Three clearly assigned parts, with light arriving from the same direction.
steps.simpleExplanation: This is a mixed force with three retained identities, not a new blended armour colour.

steps.title: Establish black and green foundations
steps.action: Paint the Iron Hands and Raven Guard parts with Abaddon Black, and the Salamanders part with Waaagh! Flesh.
steps.detail: Build smooth thin coats and allow each to dry. Leave the deepest joins dark on the green part. Matching surface quality matters more than making the colours equally bright; the green should remain visibly different from the two black panels.
steps.lookFor: Two smooth black foundations and one distinct muted green foundation.
steps.simpleExplanation: Keep the starting surfaces equally smooth while preserving the different Legion colours.

steps.title: Shade the green panel locally
steps.action: Place Athonian Camoshade in the Salamanders panel’s recessed edges.
steps.detail: Keep the wash off the broad green face and absorb any pool before it dries. The black parts already have their darkest value; leave their plate centres untouched rather than coating all three pieces with one wash.
steps.lookFor: The green panel has defined recesses while both black panels stay clean.
steps.simpleExplanation: Shade only the part that needs it, rather than treating every colour identically.

steps.title: Give the Iron Hands exposed steel
steps.action: Place small Ironbreaker marks on selected upper edges of the Iron Hands part.
steps.detail: Make these short, interrupted metallic marks on exposed contact points. Preserve most of the black surface. This compact exercise suggests worn black armour; it is not the complete blackened-metal workflow in the dedicated Iron Hands guide.
steps.lookFor: Sparse reflective steel separates this black panel from the Raven Guard panel.
steps.simpleExplanation: Use a little actual metallic paint to distinguish worn iron from painted edge light.

steps.title: Give the Raven Guard cooler painted light
steps.action: Trace Dark Reaper on the Raven Guard panel’s upper rim, then add smaller Thunderhawk Blue accents.
steps.detail: Follow the same light direction used on the Iron Hands part, but keep these lines smooth rather than chipped. Leave the centre black. If a pale line grows too wide, narrow it with Abaddon Black once dry.
steps.lookFor: Cool painted edges distinguish the Raven Guard part from the metallic Iron Hands treatment.
steps.simpleExplanation: The direction of light matches, while the material treatment stays different.

steps.title: Give the Salamanders muted green light
steps.action: Highlight the Salamanders panel with Elysian Green and a few finer Ogryn Camo accents.
steps.detail: Keep the upper rim brighter and the lower-facing edge quieter, matching the other two pieces. Restrict the pale green to narrow edges so the main armour remains muted green rather than becoming a light khaki panel.
steps.lookFor: The green panel shares the others’ light direction without losing its own colour.
steps.simpleExplanation: Match where the light falls, not the colour of the highlights.

steps.title: Connect the campaign through restraint
steps.action: Use a few tiny Rhinox Hide marks at exposed lower contact points on each part.
steps.detail: Repeat the scale and placement logic of the wear, not an identical stamp. Dark brown will be quieter on black than on green, which is expected. Stop before the wear overwhelms either black surface or turns the green mottled.
steps.lookFor: The pieces share a level of wear, while their original colours remain dominant.
steps.simpleExplanation: A similar amount of wear can connect different palettes without repainting their identities.

steps.title: Read the three pieces together
steps.action: Place the finished studies side by side and compare them at arm’s length.
steps.detail: Check that all three pieces agree on light direction and the scale of the marks, while black steel, cool black and muted green remain different. Use Abaddon Black or Waaagh! Flesh to narrow any excessive wear. Separate Legion markings and a shared basing approach can be developed later.
steps.lookFor: Three recognisable colour treatments feel part of the same campaign.
steps.simpleExplanation: Coherence comes from shared handling, not a fictional universal Shattered Legions colour scheme.
